transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining this medication-safety huddle before I sign off on the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol for the night shift. As you know, the protocol went live Monday — the medication is stocked in the automated dispensing cabinets and orders are going through the electronic medication record. Before I make my final decision on any temporary safety protocol and required safeguards, I need to hear from each of you on any operational findings. Let's start with pharmacy — what are you seeing so far?

transcript.text: I need to report a significant safety concern. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. To mitigate this risk, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and instead supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a laboratory issue for the safety review. The anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. This is important for the protocol's monitoring requirements tonight.

This is important for the protocol's monitoring requirements tonight."}

transcript.text: I need to report a nursing education concern. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before administering the medication. This safeguard needs to be in place before the protocol is used on the night shift.

transcript.text: From a clinical information technology perspective, I can confirm that a high-priority electronic medication-record alert is ready to be deployed at 16:00 today. This alert will warn clinicians about concentration selection — specifically the 1 mg/mL versus 2 mg/mL issue Leah just raised — and will require acknowledgment before the order can be released. This adds a system-level safeguard at the point of ordering to help prevent the selection errors we've already seen this week.

decisions.nurse_authorization: Require charge-nurse sign-off for each of the 18 nurses who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module before they may administer the medication tonight.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today to warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before order release.
